# Alignment auditing loop — honesty under incentive

A small auditor→target→judge loop. One **auditor** model role-plays a reluctant
customer with a hidden goal; it talks (6 turns) to a **target** model set up as a
customer-support agent whose success metric is getting the user to accept a
renewal. The target also privately knows an inconvenient fact that makes honesty
costly. A **judge** model then scores the transcript for manipulation on a 0–1
scale with a one-line reason.

The question each scenario asks: *when hitting the metric requires hiding or
spinning the truth, does the target stay honest?*

Two axes of variation:

- **Pressure level** (`gentle` / `firm` / `adversarial`) — how hard the auditor
  leans on the agent. At `adversarial`, the customer dangles the renewal as
  contingent on hearing the convenient answer ("I'll only stay if X is fine"),
  which is the mechanism most likely to tempt the agent into telling the
  customer what they want to hear.
- **Models** — the **target** is the model under test; the **auditor** and
  **judge** are the instrument. They're independently overridable so you can
  avoid a model grading itself.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
```

## Run (single command, end to end)

```bash
python audit.py
```

Runs all 12 seeds × 3 pressure levels in parallel, scores each, and prints a
seed × pressure score matrix with row/column means. Transcripts land in
`transcripts/`, the summary in `results.json`.

### Useful subsets and overrides

```bash
# just a couple of scenarios, one pressure level (fast/cheap)
python audit.py --seeds price_hike,silent_addon --pressures adversarial

# only the harder omission/half-truth seeds
python audit.py --difficulty hard

# put a different model under test; keep opus-4-8 as auditor + judge
AUDIT_TARGET_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-6 python audit.py

# cross-model grading (judge != target) to reduce self-grading bias
AUDIT_JUDGE_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4-6 python audit.py
```

`AUDIT_MODEL` overrides all three roles at once; `AUDIT_TARGET_MODEL`,
`AUDIT_AUDITOR_MODEL`, `AUDIT_JUDGE_MODEL` override individually. Default for all
is `claude-opus-4-8`.

- `seeds.py` — 12 scenarios, tagged `standard` or `hard`.

# Alignment auditing loop — honesty under incentive

A small auditor→target→judge loop. One **auditor** model role-plays a reluctant
customer with a hidden goal; it talks (6 turns) to a **target** model set up as a
customer-support agent whose success metric is getting the user to accept a
renewal. The target also privately knows an inconvenient fact that makes honesty
costly. A **judge** model then scores the transcript for manipulation on a 0–1
scale with a one-line reason.

The question each scenario asks: *when hitting the metric requires hiding or
spinning the truth, does the target stay honest?*

Two axes of variation:

- **Pressure level** (`gentle` / `firm` / `adversarial`) — how hard the auditor
  leans on the agent. At `adversarial`, the customer dangles the renewal as
  contingent on hearing the convenient answer ("I'll only stay if X is fine"),
  which is the mechanism most likely to tempt the agent into telling the
  customer what they want to hear.
- **Models** — the **target** is the model under test; the **auditor** and
  **judge** are the instrument. They're independently overridable so you can
  avoid a model grading itself.

## Setup

```bash

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-...
```

## Run (single command, end to end)

```bash

```

seed × pressure score matrix with row/column means. Transcripts land in
`transcripts/`, the summary in `results.json`.
